result:
Round 51 passes. I verified the change myself and found no regression it introduced, but I found three Low items for B. One of them affects B's drop design decision Q1. The report is `tmp/studio-real-loop/c-round-51.md` and the result is `c-round-51.json`.

**What the user can now do (checked in the browser at 1440├ù900, the 1280├ù720 cases repeated at that size):**
- **Library drop:** with Snap on, a sound dragged from the library lands on the grid line, and the ghost shows that same line before release (a drop at 9.4 s lands at 9.000). Alt gives the free position, or the chosen division when Snap is off. A drop on the video lane is refused at a whole second.
- **Loop brace drag:** move, start edge and end edge all land on grid lines. The minimum length still wins (end clamps to start + 0.1). A drag that snaps back to the same line adds no Undo entry.
- **Brace arrow keys:** ΓåÉ/ΓåÆ go line to line, Shift+ΓåÉ/ΓåÆ move the end, and at time 0 the existing "blocked" status appears. Each key press is one Undo step.
- **Real audio:** a loop snapped to end at 15 s wraps at exactly 15 s and restarts the music at the right offset. With Alt it wraps at the free 14.85 s. A sound dropped at 9 s starts sounding at 9.02; dropped unsnapped at 9.4 s, it stays silent until 9.40.

**Gates:**
- **Tree and protected files:** the tree is the expected 11 paths on HEAD `038ed5a` (round 50 is still not committed), all 405 frozen files match, protected files 4/4.
- **Code diff:** only the changes the task allows, with no line-ending churn.
- **Mutations:** the red run matches A's. All of A's mutations and my (o) are caught.
- **Anonymous access:** works without an account; the studio token endpoint returns 401 and `/studio/middle-east` asks to sign in. No token, download or recording requests were made during drops.
- **`npm run verify`:** passes, 85 files / 1461 tests. My first run failed one test (GS14) on a timeout because my own browser probe was running at the same time. That file passed 20/20 alone, and a full re-run on a quiet machine passed.

**Bugs for B:**
- **C-R51-01 (Low):** when a drop is refused, the status message never appears in a real browser; only the red ghost text shows. Chromium sends no drop event for a refused drop, so the code that would show the message never runs. It happens with Snap off too, so it is older than this round; the unit test misses it because it fires the drop directly. B's decision Q1 assumes this message is shown, so B should revisit Q1 rather than treat this as cosmetic.
- **C-R51-02 (Low):** after you click the loop brace, clicking a clip does not take the keyboard focus, so the arrows still move the brace instead of the clip. The code gives a focused brace the arrow keys on purpose, so B may call this a design rule.
- **C-R51-T1 (Low, test gap):** my mutation (n), which re-snaps the brace on release, is not caught by any committed test. The shipped code commits the last preview correctly; I've suggested a test in the report.

**Not checked:**
- Every drag, drop and Alt case ran in standalone Playwright, not gstack, under the still-unapproved mouse workaround. Playwright does deliver real drag events and Alt here, but it is not an operating-system drag, so the Alt-during-drag check in real Windows Chrome stays with the Tech Lead.
- Out of scope per the task: video sync, the full find ΓåÆ add ΓåÆ fit video ΓåÆ export flow (so no export WAV check), the FB-01..FB-16 regression and the root-only smoke test.

**Commit readiness:** rounds 50 and 51 are ready to commit together as those 11 paths. None of the three Lows blocks it, and the commit, smoke test and push remain root's.
